en.name: Garland chrysanthemum
en.summary: Garland chrysanthemum is the fragrant, deeply lobed green that goes into hotpot and is stir-fried alone with garlic. No duration is published for it, so treat it like spinach: about 3–5 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: This is one of the most fragile greens in the market and it has no room-temperature life to speak of. The leaves are thin and aromatic, they wilt within a couple of hours in a warm kitchen, and once bruised they go slimy very fast. No pantry figure is given and none should be assumed. Buy it on the day you plan to cook it if you possibly can.
en.fridge: The documented method is to rinse it quickly, drain it well, bag it and stand it stem-down in the bottom drawer of the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — standing it upright stops the stems bending and bruising. About 3–5 days is the working limit, borrowed from spinach, since the method is documented but the duration is not. Drain it properly after that rinse: water left on the leaves is exactly what makes them go slimy, and this green goes faster than most.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for garland chrysanthemum and freezing it is not worth doing. Its entire appeal is the aroma, which is carried in volatile compounds that do not survive freezing and thawing, and the thin leaves collapse anyway. If you have too much, cook it now — it wilts down to almost nothing and is perfectly good cold the next day dressed with sesame.
spoilage: Slimy, blackened or translucent leaves, especially where they were pressed
Yellowing leaves, or stems gone soft and bendy
A sour or muddy smell instead of the usual strong herbal scent
Liquid pooling in the bottom of the bag
tips: Choose bunches with springy, deeply cut leaves and firm pale stems.
Drain thoroughly after rinsing and store the bunch standing up.
Add it to hotpot at the very end — thirty seconds is enough.
Use the thicker stems too; sliced thin they are crisp and taste of the same thing.

faq.q: How long does garland chrysanthemum last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, rinsed, drained, bagged and stood stem-down. That figure is borrowed from spinach; none is published for this green.
There is no timeline and no point. The aroma is the whole reason to buy it, and freezing destroys the volatile compounds that carry it.

faq.q: Why does it go slimy so quickly?
faq.a: Thin leaves plus trapped water. Drain it really well before bagging and keep the bunch loose rather than crushed.

faq.q: Can you eat garland chrysanthemum raw?
faq.a: Young leaves are good raw in a salad, though the flavour is strong. Older, larger leaves are better wilted briefly in a hotpot or a hot pan.

zh.name: 茼蒿
zh.summary: 茼蒿是香氣濃郁、葉緣深裂的葉菜，火鍋裡少不了它，單炒蒜末也很好吃。它沒有公布的保存天數，可以比照菠菜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 3～5 天。
zh.pantry: 茼蒿是市場上最嬌嫩的葉菜之一，根本沒有常溫保存這回事。葉片又薄又香，在溫暖的廚房裡兩三個小時就萎了，一旦壓傷更是很快變黏。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。可以的話，當天要煮再買。
zh.fridge: 有依據的做法是：快速沖洗、確實瀝乾、裝袋後根部朝下立放在冰箱下層抽屜，維持 4°C 以下——立著放可以避免莖被壓彎壓傷。約 3～5 天是工作上限，這是比照菠菜而來，因為方法有依據、天數則沒有。沖洗後務必徹底瀝乾：留在葉片上的水正是讓它變黏的原因，而茼蒿變黏的速度比多數葉菜都快。
zh.freezer: 茼蒿沒有冷凍保存期限，而且冷凍不值得。它的價值全在香氣，而香氣來自揮發性成分，經過冷凍解凍就所剩無幾，薄葉本身也一定會塌掉。真的太多的話，現在就煮吧——它一炒就縮得很少，隔天用胡麻醬拌成冷菜也很好吃。
spoilage: 葉片黏滑、發黑或變得半透明，尤其是被壓到的地方
葉子泛黃，或莖變軟可彎
有酸味或土味，而不是原本濃郁的草本香氣
tips: 挑葉片有彈性、裂口深、莖結實淡綠的。
沖洗後徹底瀝乾，整把立著保存。
火鍋請在最後才下，三十秒就夠了。
粗莖也別丟，切細後又脆又香，味道是一樣的。

faq.q: 茼蒿放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏，沖洗瀝乾後裝袋、根部朝下立放，約 3～5 天。這個數字是比照菠菜而來；茼蒿本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也沒有意義。香氣是買它的全部理由，而冷凍會破壞承載香氣的揮發性成分。

faq.q: 茼蒿為什麼這麼快變黏？
faq.a: 葉薄加上留住水分。裝袋前務必徹底瀝乾，整把鬆鬆放好不要壓實。
嫩葉可以做沙拉，只是味道很濃。比較老、比較大的葉子還是丟火鍋或下熱鍋快燙一下比較好。
